extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A dataset for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models, consisting of 506 challenging instruction-response instances across eight visual scenarios.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan; Hritik Bansal; Kai-Wei Chang; Nanyun Peng
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built as image-instruction-response triplets requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements. Images were sourced from multiple existing datasets and web sources, filtered manually or heuristically, annotated by the authors in two groups following guidelines, and then verified by MTurk workers and cross-reviewed by the author groups.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the verification stage, MTurk workers found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. The incorrect samples were filtered out before finalizing the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, screenshots from OpenWebText links, and test sets of InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Existing VQA dataset images were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs and categorized into Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes groups.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images in Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract were manually filtered for suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, PaddleOCR was used to detect text and the top 500 images with the highest number of words were selected, with a subset annotated. Incorrect samples found during verification were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors created human-written instructions and ground-truth responses under annotation guidelines, with each author group assigned four categories. MTurk workers then verified each image-instruction-response sample, and author groups reviewed each other's samples. The paper also notes additional annotations for whether samples require information extraction and mathematical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification by MTurk workers found that 96% of samples were annotated correctly; incorrect samples were filtered out and then cross-reviewed by the author groups.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for human evaluation of predicted responses; 1 for dataset sample verification
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors; MTurk workers mainly from the US for human baseline and evaluation
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (including PP-OCRv4), CLIP-retrieval UI, ShareGPT-4V-7B for dense image captions, GPT-4V for synthetic instruction-response generation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples will be released as a validation set with reference responses, while responses for the remaining 406 samples are hidden; the project also includes a continuously updated leaderboard.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator geography/region (mainly from the US); linguistic diversity and writing style are discussed as varying across social groups.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to assess multimodal reasoning on text-rich images with real-world applications such as assisting the visually impaired and understanding abstract text-rich images. The authors aimed to avoid offensive content and note that models can generate harmful or hallucinated responses, though they did not observe apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information in their experiments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human baseline and evaluation may reflect bias from annotators being mainly from the US, with linguistic diversity and writing style potentially varying across social groups; the authors suggest involving annotators from more diverse regions in future work.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MTurk workers found the annotation task time-consuming and difficult within a limited budget. The human baseline and evaluation may not generalize across social groups because annotators were mainly from the US. The released dataset hides reference responses for 406 samples.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning; model development via a 100-sample validation set; establishing human and automatic evaluation baselines.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce CONTEXTUAL, a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images.

description.evidence: To evaluate multimodal models’ capability of jointly reasoning over embedded text and visual context in text-rich images, we propose CONTEXTUAL, a Context-sensitive Text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation. CONTEXTUAL covers eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes.

url.evidence: Our dataset, code, and leaderboard can be found on the project page https://con-textual.github.io/.
